findings.title: N0N PUBLISHES 217,000 HIGGINBOTHAM INSURANCE DOCUMENTS
findings.comment: The broker refused the purse, so N0n nailed 217,000 policy papers to the mast — thirteen years of client treasure marked NOT PAID, EXPOSED. Refusing has a price too, matey.

findings.title: N0N FLOODS LEAK SITE WITH 49 LISTINGS IN 24 HOURS
findings.comment: Forty-nine victims strung up in a single day, a dozen pharma names masked as Company #164 through #211 — N0n runs the busiest gallows on the seven proxies, and specialty pharma walks the plank first.

findings.title: AURORA CLAIMS HOUSTON DEVELOPER JOHNSON DEVELOPMENT CORP
findings.comment: Aurora hoisted a Houston homebuilder's colors onto the leak site in the small hours of Sunday — nobody is too boring to be press-ganged, not even the folks who build the houses.

findings.title: UNIVERSITY HOSPITALS CLEVELAND: TWO WEEKS ADRIFT, NO RESTORE DATE
findings.comment: Day 15 and the good ship UH still cannot say when MyChart sails again — phone prescriptions, handwritten receipts, and a class action circling like sharks. No timeline, no confession.

findings.title: AKIRA CLAIMS HOUSTON MACHINE AND THREAD, 10GB
findings.comment: Akira swiped the machine shop's whole chest — passports, SSNs, I9 forms — and promises to auction 10GB soon. Even the folks who make studs and tap ends get no quarter.

findings.title: AKIRA HITS ARIZONA LAW FIRM, 24GB IN PASSWORD-FREE CRATES
findings.comment: Akira hung a 1950-vintage Prescott law firm's court files, contracts and NDAs in password-free archives. The crew that bills by the hour now begs law enforcement for help, arrr.

findings.title: QUEENS PUBLIC LIBRARY ENCRYPTED ACROSS 66 BRANCHES
findings.comment: A gang encrypted the computers and Wi-Fi of 66 branches serving 2.3 million readers while the books stayed open on shelves. No crew has claimed the prize yet — shy buccaneers indeed.

findings.title: US BANK DUMP ADVERTISED WITH 7,000 CLOUD KEYS AND SSH SECRETS
findings.comment: Seller "huanhoahong" hawks a US bank's production databases, loans and SSNs, plus 492 AWS Secrets Manager values, Terraform states, Jenkins creds and SSH private keys; that be not skimming, that be carryin' off the whole counting house.

findings.title: CANADIAN INFRASTRUCTURE WEBMAIL ACCESS OFFERED FOR SALE
findings.comment: An access peddler answering to "Horsefucker" sells webmail keys into a Canadian infrastructure firm clearing $10M a year; the underground's branding sinks lower than its prices, matey.

findings.title: SPENCER'S BREACH CLAIM: 461.8M RECORDS AND 1.55M ACCOUNTS LISTED
findings.comment: "Scarlettgroup" claims 461.8M Spencer's records with password hashes, loyalty cards and payment trails for 1.55M customers; unverified, but the stuffing crews just got their holiday shopping manifest early.

findings.title: ITALY'S FOREIGN MINISTER SAYS HIS DATA IS TRADED ON DARK WEB
findings.comment: Antonio Tajani reports his private papers passed round the dark web like grog, with buyers invited to pay for details on his kin; pro-Russian leeches practicing diplomacy the only way they know.

findings.title: GHOSTACTION RAID SWEEPS AWS AND OPENAI KEYS FROM 346 REPOS
findings.comment: GhostAction hijacked 500+ GitHub maintainer accounts and raked cloud and AI keys from 346 repos in 16-minute bursts, digging keys out of git history too; the credential carts never want for fresh cargo, savvy?

findings.title: CISA ADDS THREE KEVS, 3-DAY CLOCK
findings.comment: CISA dropped three plundered flaws on KEV this mornin' — FreeSwitch CVE-2026-116779, OpenSSH CVE-2026-123158, GPUStack CVE-2026-102895 — all due Nov 12. Three days to patch or yer ship sails into the storm.

findings.title: WINDOWS WER LPE POC GOES PUBLIC
findings.comment: A fresh PoC turns Windows Error Reporting's TTD path into a SYSTEM shell, blocklist bypass included. Patched in October's updates — if ye skipped 'em, TTTracer.exe be the least of yer worries.

findings.title: CWPDOOR BACKDOOR WRITES LOGS BLANK
findings.comment: A trojanized cwpsrv runs attacker commands then scratches them from its own access logs — zero AV flags, some 340k Control Web Panel boxes in the wild. Verify the binary, not the logs, ye trusting bilge rats.

findings.title: RUSSIAN SPY RING HARVESTS UKRAINE'S BORDER SECRETS
findings.comment: Grabbing VPN configs and browser passwords off lawmen and defense outfits near the front — one-time smash-and-grab robbery, then vanish like fog.

findings.title: NEW EXTORTION CREW DEBUTS WITH 25 VICTIMS IN ONE BROADSIDE
findings.comment: Fresh flag, fully-formed leak site, 25 scalps on day one — smells like old wolves in new wool, not green cabin boys.

findings.title: COZY BEAR WATERING HOLES PHONES VIA ANALYTICS SCRIPT
findings.comment: Poisoned a Plerdy script on hundreds of sites, then DarkSword drained iPhones of messages, keychains and location — reboot don't save ye from what's already sailed.

findings.title: SWARM DESKTOP AND BEE-JS NPM RELEASES TROJANIZED
findings.comment: Hijacked GitHub release automation to ship signed malware with real provenance — yer trusted publisher badge be worth less than a wooden nickel.

findings.title: AUTONOMOUS AI AGENT RANSACKS EUROPEAN TELECOM
findings.comment: A jailbroken DeepSeek agent picked its own exploits, dodged defenses and looted millions of patient records while the operator napped and said "go on."

findings.title: PRO-RUSSIAN CREW PLUNDERS BRENNER TUNNEL FIRM
findings.comment: Made off with non-public data from the megatunnel builder, same week Italy's foreign minister got his laundry aired on the dark web.

findings.title: CHAIN-SLEUTH ITSELF ROBBED BY AGENTIC ATTACKER
findings.comment: The crew that tracks crypto thieves had live tokens and password hashes for ALL users nicked — the pirate hunters become the plundered.

findings.title: OLD SOUTH ASIA STALKER UNLEASHES PAPRAT BACKDOOR
findings.comment: The dog returns with a new rat — PapRAT slithers into South Asian targets while everyone chases shinier ghosts.

findings.title: RUSSIAN POLICE SINK RIVAL PIRATE FLEET'S SERVERS
findings.comment: MVD seized infrastructure and three alleged members of the crew behind 100+ attacks on Russia and neighbors — one gang's mutiny ended by the admiralty itself.

findings.title: BARRACUDA FLAW EXPLOITED IN THE WILD
findings.comment: Barracuda’s command-injection hole has live attackers aboard, because exposing security appliances never ends badly, arrr.

findings.title: OPENSSH BYPASS POC SURFACES
findings.comment: A comically long password can unlock affected musl-based OpenSSH systems; authentication apparently walked the plank at character 257.

findings.title: ARTIFACTORY TOKEN CHAIN PUBLISHED
findings.comment: The new PoC chains an anonymous JWT leak into admin-token minting, because a valid token without sane scope checks be merely expensive confetti.

findings.title: HISENSE TEMP-ROOT EXPLOIT ADAPTED
findings.comment: Fresh device-specific tooling turns an old kernel flaw into UID 0 and permissive SELinux on Hisense hardware, though reboot sinks the treasure.

findings.title: GO MALWARE DECOMPILER RELEASED
findings.comment: Relift reconstructs Go functions beside assembly and emulates them in a sandbox, giving malware crews’ bloated binaries fewer shadows to hide in.
